annotation.kind: source selection, tier label, and scaled-orthogonal real-equivalent formalization of the final backward-error construction

assumptions: The real-equivalent normalized Fourier action is orthogonal.
The unnormalized transform scale is positive.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P09 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P09 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p09_t2_scaled_orthogonal_backward_error {n : Nat} (Q : Fin n -> Fin n -> Real) (e : Fin n -> Real) (s : Real) (hs : 0 < s) (hQ : p09Orthogonal Q) : exists delta, p09MatVec (p09ScaleMatrix s Q) delta = e and p09VecNorm2 delta = p09VecNorm2 e / s and p09Max delta <= p09VecNorm2 delta
formal_statement.plain_language: Every output error of a positively scaled orthogonal transform is exactly the transform of a fictional input perturbation with the expected norm scaling.

informal_proof: Choose delta as one over the scale times the transpose action on the output error. Orthogonality gives exact recovery and preserves the Euclidean norm; scalar homogeneity and the infinity-versus-Euclidean bound give the two certificates.
informal_statement: The exact fictional-input backward-error certificate stated in the paper's conclusion, for the normalized real-equivalent Fourier action.

paper_source.local_path: paper_bencmark/reference_papers/P09_Roundoff Error Analysis of the Fast Fourier Transform.pdf

paper_version: published journal version; volume 25, issue 116, October 1971, printed pages 757-768

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: The frozen baseline supplies the inverse-action, orthogonal-isometry, homogeneity, and max/Euclidean pieces separately, but no declaration constructs Ramos's scaled backward perturbation.

source_locations.anchor: prose assertion e = T delta and the two following unnumbered bounds
source_locations.role: fictional input perturbation and its norm certificates

tier_rationale: The L proof combines NumStability.matMulVec_of_isRightInverse, NumStability.vecNorm2_smul, NumStability.vecNorm2_orthogonal, and NumStability.infNormVec_le_vecNorm2 from NumStability/Analysis/MatrixAlgebra.lean with the paper-specific scaled-transpose construction.
